entities.name: PMID:25424708
observations: In 2,082 tertiary headache-clinic adults, women had longer and more intense migraine attacks than men in migraine with and without aura; nausea, photophobia, and phonophobia were generally more common in women. Age-related changes appeared in female patients after age 30, while no age-dependent variation was observed in male patients. Abstract lacks interaction coefficients and age-stratum effect sizes.

entities.name: PMID:16866720
observations: In 1,009 patients aged 16–80, increasing age was associated overall with fewer headache days, fewer moderate/severe days, less aura, photophobia, phonophobia, dizziness, activity aggravation, and recurrence, with improved function and acute-medication response. Nausea, vomiting, average intensity, and attack duration did not significantly differ by age overall; no formal sex-by-age interaction was reported.

entities.name: PMID:36942410
observations: In a prospective electronic-diary cohort of 1,347 women and 284 men, attacks were longer in women than men; adjusted duration ratios were 1.15 for non-perimenstrual and 1.62 for perimenstrual attacks. Women had more photophobia, phonophobia, and nausea but less aura. Age was an adjustment variable, not a tested sex-by-age interaction.

entities.name: PMID:35679008
observations: Review evidence indicates migraine is generally more prevalent, frequent, and disabling in women, with more nausea, photophobia, and phonophobia, and emphasizes hormonal transitions across the life course. It does not provide a pooled sex-by-age interaction estimate.

entities.name: PMID:35013446
observations: In a Korean population study, visual aura was associated with higher monthly headache frequency, but the available report did not provide a sex-by-age interaction.
